title: When Do Breast Augmentation Stitches Dissolve?
meta_description: When Do Breast Augmentation Stitches Dissolve? How long stitches take to dissolve, what healing looks like, and how to care for your incisions.
excerpt: Visible stitch ends often fade within 1 to 2 weeks, but buried sutures take about 2 to 8 months to absorb, depending on the material. Here is the timeline by suture type, what a poking stitch means, and when to call your surgeon.
quick_answer:
When do breast augmentation stitches dissolve?

Visible stitch ends often fade within 1 to 2 weeks, in line with Cleveland Clinic, but buried material takes longer: about 56 to 70 days for Coated Vicryl Plus, 91 to 119 days for Monocryl and 182 to 238 days for PDS, by the makers' figures. Stitches that need removing come out in about a week to two weeks.

Dissolvable Stitches Timeline After Breast Augmentation
1 to 2 weeks: Visible stitch ends often fade
About 2 months: Coated Vicryl Plus fully absorbed (56 to 70 days)
3 to 4 months: Monocryl fully absorbed (91 to 119 days)
6 to 8 months: PDS essentially complete (182 to 238 days)
Sources: Cleveland Clinic, suture makers' data. Your surgeon's suture may differ.

Healing Stitches: Normal vs Call Your Surgeon
Normal
Incision lines flatten and fade
Less redness each week
A little itching or tingling
Tape falling off on its own
Call your surgeon
Pus or bad-smelling drainage
Spreading redness or heat
An incision or stitch line that opens
A new lump or growing pain
Fever or chills
Sources: Cleveland Clinic, MedlinePlus, UW Medicine.

quotes: It usually takes one to two weeks before absorbable stitches dissolve. These stitches can last for a few months, depending on how your body heals.

quotes: On average, full recovery takes about six to eight weeks.

Increasing enlargement, or firmness, of one or both of your breasts that’s associated with pain and pressure.

sources.title: Breast Augmentation - Aftercare & Recovery
quotes: It typically takes one to two weeks to recover from a breast augmentation.

If the pain is extreme or long-lasting, contact your surgeon.
If you have external sutures, your surgeon will remove them in about a week. If your surgeon used tissue glue or tape, it will fall off on its own in a week or two.

Rest and sleep on your back in an inclined position (25-to 45-degree angle) for the initial postoperative days or if you have significant swelling. Use wedge pillows with an incline design or sleep in a recliner chair.

sources.title: Recovering from Breast Reduction & Breast Augmentation
quotes: You may experience some asymmetry since each breast may heal at a different rate.
You will begin to notice your final results around three months after surgery. However, you may continue to have subtle changes throughout the 12 months following your surgery.
You may feel shooting pains, tingling, or other strange sensations in your skin for the first few months.
For the first week after surgery, you should rest and sleep on your back, with extra pillows to prop you up. This can help with swelling.
Do not sleep on your stomach until your surgeon says it’s okay. If you want to sleep on your side, you should:
wait until three to four weeks after surgery and
alternate sides at first to help with swelling.
You will wear a surgical bra for three to four weeks after your surgery. You should only remove the bra to shower or to wash it.
After three to four weeks of wearing the surgical bra, you can transition into a soft, supportive sports bra.
You can resume a daily shower two days after surgery. Do not soak in a bathtub, pool, or hot tub until your incisions heal or your surgeon says it’s okay.
